questions.q: Why does the lesson commit before every zudojs generate?
questions.explain: The CLI does not look at git at all. The commit is for you: a known starting point makes the generator's changes visible and reversible, which is how the lesson undid the accidental availability module in one line.
options: The CLI refuses to generate in a repository with uncommitted changes
A generate edits several files at once; with a clean commit, git diff shows exactly what it did and git restore plus git clean undo it
Generated files are only type-checked after a commit
The manifest records the commit hash of every generation

questions.q: zudojs generate module scheduling --dry-run listed 7 files; the real run wrote 8. What was the extra change?
questions.explain: The real run also registered new SchedulingModule() in src/app.ts. A dry run is a close preview, not a contract, so read git diff after the real run.
options: src/app.ts, where the new module was added to the runtime's list of modules

questions.q: In a modular-monolith project, what does zudojs generate service availability --module scheduling do?
questions.explain: The CLI maps service to module for this architecture and says so on one line. Because the exit code is 0, a script would not notice. Undo it and write the service inside the module yourself.
options: Refuses, because service is only for microservice projects
Creates a whole new module src/modules/availability/, registers it with the runtime and the router, ignores --module, and exits with 0
Writes a service in the shared src/services/ folder

questions.q: Which part of that run is the clearest sign that something unexpected happened?
questions.explain: The mapping line and the paths are the only signals. The architecture line is correct, 8 files is normal for a module, and the exit code is 0.
options: Mapping "service" → "module" for modular-monolith architecture. and file paths under src/modules/availability/

questions.q: You need a service class inside the scheduling module. Which approach works with the published CLI?
questions.explain: controller, repository, dto and the other schematics respect --module. Editing the manifest by hand would make every later command misread the project, and --service is for microservice projects.
options: Write it by hand in src/modules/scheduling/services/, or run generate controller … --module scheduling (which cascades to a service) and delete what you do not need
There is no way; services must live outside modules

questions.q: What is dangerous about the file zudojs generate validator booking-date writes?
questions.explain: A stub that compiles and has a convincing name is easy to wire in and forget. Search for such stubs before a release and keep a test that feeds each validator bad input.
options: It returns true for every input, yet its name, validateBookingDate, makes it look finished
It imports a package the project does not have

questions.q: Why does the booking store amountKobo: 50_000_000 instead of amountNaira: 500000.00?
questions.explain: Money in the smallest unit as an integer is exact. 0.1 + 0.2 style errors only appear with fractions, so the code keeps fractions out of every calculation.
options: Whole kobo are integers, so sums never suffer floating-point rounding; you divide by 100 only to display
The schema library has no decimal type
Naira amounts are always whole numbers

questions.q: Where does a booking's amountKobo come from?
questions.explain: The client never chooses its own price. Copying the rate into the booking also keeps old bookings at the price they were made for, even if the hall's rate changes later.
options: The request body, checked by the schema
The hall's dailyRateKobo, copied by the service when the booking is created
The controller, from a query parameter
It is computed each time a booking is read

questions.q: The server's clock runs in UTC. Why does AvailabilityService compute "today" with timeZone: "Africa/Lagos"?
questions.explain: "Today" is a local concept. The service takes it from a replaceable function, defaulting to the Lagos date, so tests can pin it to a fixed day.
options: The business works on Lagos dates; between 23:00 and midnight UTC it is already the next day in Lagos, so a UTC "today" would accept a booking for a day that has already started there
Dates in UTC cannot be compared as strings

questions.q: Where must "never book a hall twice for the same date" be enforced so that two simultaneous requests cannot both succeed?
questions.explain: Any check followed later by a write leaves a gap in which another request can pass the same check. Only the place that writes can make "check and insert" one indivisible step.
options: In the controller, before calling the service
In the service, by calling quote() and checking available
In the storage layer, where checking and inserting happen with nothing in between (no await in memory, a UNIQUE constraint in a database)

questions.q: The in-memory bookings repository refuses double bookings correctly. You run three copies of the app behind a load balancer. What happens?
questions.explain: Process memory is per process. The rule has to move to shared storage: a PostgreSQL table with UNIQUE (hall_id, date), whose violation becomes a ConflictError.
options: It still works, because the repositories share memory through the container
Each copy has its own Map, so two copies can each accept the same hall and date
The load balancer detects the conflict
The app refuses to start more than once

questions.q: The // zudojs:routes markers were deleted from a module's routes/index.ts, and you generate a new resource there. What happens?
questions.explain: Missing markers only produce a warning. Read the last lines of every generate, and keep a smoke test that builds the router the way server.ts does.
options: The command fails with exit code 1 and writes nothing
The CLI appends the lines at the end of the function instead
It writes the resource, prints Warning: Finish by hand, exits with 0; type check and the generated test pass, but the server answers 404 for the new path

questions.q: Why does tests/enquiries.test.ts pass even though the enquiries routes were never registered in the app?
questions.explain: It is a unit test of the resource. Wiring is only tested by something that builds the router from createDependencies() and registerRoutes(), like the smoke test.
options: Vitest skips tests for new resources
The generated test creates its own router and registers the enquiries routes on it directly, so it never goes through registerRoutes
The in-memory repository answers every path

questions.q: In a freshly generated project, a repository throws new Error("connection refused") during a request. What happens?
questions.explain: The generated dispatch rethrows errors that are not exposed 4xx errors, and the HTTP server answers a bare 500. The client learns nothing, which is right, but neither does the operator. createDispatch(router, logger) fixes that.
options: The client gets 500 with the message, and it is logged
The client gets 503 and the error is logged
The client gets a generic 500 and nothing is logged anywhere

questions.q: The fixed createDispatch logs unexpected errors but not NotFoundError. Why not log every error?
questions.explain: Logs are for the operator. Errors that the client caused and that the app answered correctly belong in metrics at most; errors the app could not handle need a log line with the method, path and message.
options: Logging 4xx errors would leak them to the client
A 404 or 409 is a normal answer to a client's request, not a fault; logging each one buries the real failures in noise
4xx errors are logged by the router instead

questions.q: In the generated src/app.ts, how does the runtime learn the environment?
questions.explain: So loadConfig({ NODE_ENV: "production" }) in a test gives a production config and a runtime that says test (Vitest sets NODE_ENV). Passing { NODE_ENV: options.config.nodeEnv } makes both agree.
options: From resolveEnvironment() with no argument, which reads process.env directly and ignores config.nodeEnv

questions.q: After you added a second constructor parameter to BookingsService, the old test still called it with one argument, yet npm run typecheck passed. Why?
questions.explain: Nothing type-checks the tests until you add something that does, such as tsconfig.test.json with "include": ["src/**/*", "tests/**/*"] and a typecheck:tests script.
options: The generated tsconfig.json only includes src/**/* and excludes **/*.test.ts, and Vitest strips types without checking them
The typecheck script uses --noEmit, which skips errors

questions.q: You have written real code in the bookings resource and moved its wiring out of the markers. A teammate runs zudojs generate resource bookings --module scheduling --force. What happens?
questions.explain: --force overwrites the schematic's own files and re-inserts the wiring line it cannot find. In the lesson the type checker caught the damage; a change the types cannot see would have been lost silently.
options: Nothing, because the resource already exists
Only the test file is refreshed
The DTO, repository, service, controller, routes and test are rewritten from the template, and a second bookingsController line is added between the markers
The CLI detects your changes and merges them

questions.q: What does the published CLI offer for deployment?
questions.explain: The CLI prepares; you deploy. Building and running the image, the release step and the pipeline are yours, as the deployment and CI/CD lessons show.
options: zudojs deploy, which builds and uploads the app
No deploy command (zudojs deploy exits with 3, "not found"); zudojs add docker writes a Dockerfile, .dockerignore and compose.yaml

questions.q: Where do database migrations come from in a CLI-made project?
questions.explain: zudojs migrate does not exist. Migrations are npm scripts; your release process runs db:deploy before starting the new version.
options: zudojs add database adds Prisma and npm scripts: db:migrate (prisma migrate dev) for development and db:deploy (prisma migrate deploy) for production

questions.q: The API is private, but /docs answers 200 in production. Which change uses a real mountOpenAPI option?
questions.explain: docsPath: false skips the page; middleware runs before every route mountOpenAPI registers, so you can require a secret there without touching the API routes.
options: Delete /docs from the router after starting the server
docsPath: config.nodeEnv === "production" ? false : "/docs", or a middleware that checks a key before the documentation routes

questions.q: The date schema was schema.string().refine(validateBookingDate, "…"). How did it appear in /openapi.json, and what improved it?
questions.explain: A document can describe declarative rules (types, lengths, patterns), not arbitrary functions. Put as much of a rule as possible in a publishable form, and describe the rest in words.
options: As a plain string; adding .regex(/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/) published a pattern, while the refine still runs but cannot be described
It did not appear at all
As the full source code of the validator

questions.q: Why are the halls and bookings repositories built outside the markers in src/container.ts?
questions.explain: The generator writes new Controller(new Service(new Repository())), one fresh repository per resource. AvailabilityService must read the same bookings that BookingsService writes, so the objects are built once and shared, in your part of the file.
options: Code between markers is not compiled
Two services must share the same repository objects, which the generator's one-line-per-resource wiring cannot express, and the generator must not rewrite hand-made wiring
Repositories must be created before the health check

questions.q: A customer asks for 350 guests in a hall that holds 200. Which answer does the project give, and where is it decided?
questions.explain: The schema only knows that guests is a positive integer; the capacity lives with the hall, so the service checks it. ValidationError carries status 400, and dispatch turns it into the response.
options: 400, a ValidationError thrown by the service, which knows the hall's capacity
404, because no hall is big enough

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Dividing by 100 turns kobo into naira for display, and the formatter adds the symbol, thousands separators and two decimals.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Lagos is UTC+1, so 23:30 UTC on New Year's Eve is 00:30 on 1 January there. en-CA writes the date as YYYY-MM-DD.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: JavaScript rolls the extra days over into March instead of refusing the date. That is why the validator compares the printed date with the input: 2026-03-02 is not 2026-02-30, so the date is not real.
questions.code:
const date = new Date("2026-02-30T00:00:00Z");
console.log(Number.isNaN(date.getTime()), date.toISOString().slice(0, 10));

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: The await pauses the first call after its lookup. The second call then looks, finds nothing, and pauses too. Both then insert: a double booking.

questions.q: The same two calls, but the lookup is now synchronous. What does this print?
questions.explain: An async function runs synchronously until its first await. With no await between check and push, the first call finishes both before the second starts, so the second finds the booking and throws.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Strings compare character by character. With zero-padded months, "1" vs "0" gives the right answer. Without padding, "1" is compared with "9", and December sorts before September. Plain string comparison of dates is only safe for strict YYYY-MM-DD, which is why the schema has a regex.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: The e-mail is trimmed and lower-cased before the e-mail check, and unknown fields such as price are dropped. That is how a client's attempt to send its own price disappears before the service sees it.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Each error carries its status and expose: true, which is exactly what errorResponse checks before turning an error into a response. A plain Error has neither, so it becomes a generic 500.
options:
ValidationError 400 true
NotFoundError 404 true
ConflictError 409 true

ValidationError 422 true
NotFoundError 404 true
ConflictError 409 true

ValidationError 400 false
NotFoundError 404 false
ConflictError 409 false

Error 500 false
Error 500 false
Error 500 false

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Case does not matter, and a missing NODE_ENV means development. Passing the object explicitly is what lets createApp use the value loadConfig read instead of process.env.

questions.q: A simplified version of the generator's marker insertion. What does this print?
questions.explain: Without markers the generator does not guess where the line goes; it only warns. With markers it is idempotent: a line already present is not added again.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Parsing both dates as UTC midnight makes every day exactly 86,400,000 ms long, so the difference is a whole number of days even across a year boundary.

questions.q: A booking attempt against rules checked in this order. What does this print?
questions.explain: The first failing rule decides the answer. A request that breaks two rules gets the status of the rule checked first, which is why the order of checks in the service is part of the API's behaviour.

questions.q: Write validateBookingDate(input): true only for a string in the form YYYY-MM-DD that is a real calendar date.
questions.explain: Check the type and the shape first, then round-trip: parse as UTC midnight and print it back. A date JavaScript had to roll over (30 February becomes 2 March) no longer matches the input.

questions.q: Write formatKobo(kobo) that shows an integer amount of kobo as naira with Intl.NumberFormat (en-NG, currency NGN).
questions.explain: Create the formatter once and reuse it. The division happens only at the edge, for display; all arithmetic stays in integer kobo.

questions.q: Write lagosDate(instant) that returns the calendar date in Lagos for a Date, as YYYY-MM-DD.
questions.explain: Name the time zone explicitly so the answer does not depend on the machine the code runs on. At 23:00 UTC it is midnight in Lagos, the start of the next day.

questions.q: Finish create so that two simultaneous calls for the same hall and date cannot both succeed: throw new Error("taken") for the second. Do not put an await between the check and the insert.
questions.explain: The whole check-and-insert runs before the function's first pause, so the second call sees the first booking. In a database the same guarantee comes from a UNIQUE (hall_id, date) constraint.

questions.q: Write canCancel(date, today): true when the booking date is at least 7 days after today. Both are YYYY-MM-DD strings.
questions.explain: Exactly 7 days away is allowed, 6 is not: test both boundaries. Taking today as a parameter keeps the function pure and testable.

questions.q: A smoke test knows the paths the app must serve. Write missingRoutes(expected, answer), where answer(path) returns a status code, that returns the paths answered with 404.
questions.explain: That is the idea of the smoke test in one line: request each path the assembled app should serve and report the ones nobody answers. The real test does it through registerRoutes and createDependencies.

questions.q: Write handleError(error, log): if the error has a numeric statusCode from 400 to 499 and expose === true, return that status without logging. Otherwise call log(error.message) and return 500.
questions.explain: Only errors that are both client errors and marked safe to show become their own answer. Everything else is logged for the operator and answered with a generic 500, which is what createDispatch adds to the generated dispatch.
questions.expected:
404
logged: connection refused: 10.0.0.5:5432
500
logged: internal detail
500

questions.q: Write checkGuests(guests, capacity) that throws new Error(`The hall holds ${capacity} guests, not ${guests}.`) when there are too many guests, and returns nothing otherwise.
questions.explain: A full hall is allowed; one more guest is not. In the project the service throws a ValidationError, so the same check also gives the client a 400 with this message.
questions.expected:
150 ok
200 ok
201 The hall holds 200 guests, not 201.
